basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 59.' and it opens '(Vers. 59.) Et dimiserunt Rebeccam sororem suam, et substantiam ejus, et servum Abraham,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 59.) Et dimiserunt Rebeccam sororem suam, et substantiam ejus, et servum Abraham, et viros qu cum eo erant. In Hebraeo habet: Et dimiserunt Rebeccam sororem suam, et nutricem ejus, et servum Abrahae, et viros illius. Decens quippe erat, ut ad nuptias absque parentibus virgo proficiscens, nutricis solatio foveretur.
